verdicts.reason: Viewed the recorded 100 ms playback as a sequence at native 1x and nearest 3x on #172336 across four complete cycles, including every fourth-to-first wrap (transitions 04, 08, 12, 16). The loop is one continuous activity: each of the four steps, the wrap included, is the same quarter-turn clockwise increment of the same three-segment ring, so there is no visible jump, reversal or hold at the wrap. Center/anchor is stable: the ring turns about the cell center, every frame occupies an 11x11 box offset by at most one pixel, and nothing drifts or slides. Visual volume is stable: 32 opaque pixels, the same cluster shapes and the same blue ramp in every frame; no morphing or shrinking segment. Pacing is even: equal 90-degree steps at measured 99.9-100.1 ms intervals, no near-hold. The remaining quality note is a design choice, not a defect: the three segments carry unequal weight (bar, slim vertical, heavier curved piece), which gives the spinner a slight visual lope, but it reads clearly as deliberate rotating activity at both scales. Judgment is mine from the viewed exposures and my enlargements; the timing files were read only as supporting measurements.
